questions.question: Case study 01: Mr. Chandrakant Kini is the manager of GE Appliance division, each April, he must evaluate all his subordinates to decide who is to receive a merit increase for the next fiscal year. But each year these employees complain about how they are evaluated, how merit money is dispersed, and what criteria are used for evaluations. However, during the past two years there has been a tremendous emphasis on quality of production. A review of the merit recipients reveals that these people were the ones who had the best quality records. But many of the employees felt that quality should not be the determining factor. At an employee forum, one of the senior members remarked: “How can Mr. Kini now reward quality? What has happened to production numbers?” Another employee agreed and stated: “This quality game is okay for some, but what about overall production? It seems to me that if I will only be rewarded for quality, then I should produce a few items but make them perfect.” After hearing such criticism, Mr. Kini was quite upset. He was not trying to cause chaos in his evaluations, nor was he attempting to hurt anyone. Unfortunately, what was originally intended to be an evaluation system had just become a nuisance. Answer the following questions: a. What is the major problem with Mr. Kini’s evaluation system? (02) b. Describe a performance evaluation system that you could recommend (03) Mr. Kini and justify its need. c. What does the above case tell us about the impact of performance (02) appraisals on employee motivation? d. If no changes are made in the current system that you could (03) recommend to Mr. Kini, what do you expect will occur regarding the future production performance of the employees? (HSS-318) Page 1 of 3

questions.question: Case Study 05: Raju was an apprentice trainee in a large public sector project, While on job during the training period he was involved in a fatal accident. He was not a member of the union. Still the union took up his case and asked for funeral advance. When the management was hesitant to take an immediate decision, the union threatened the management with a wildcat strike. The management paid the advance. Two days later the union insisted that the management must pay compensation as per Workman’s Compensation Act. The management maintained that, at the time of this death, Raju was not an employee and so he was not eligible for compensation. The management was afraid it would set a precedent. The compensation worked out to Rs. 20,000. The union maintained that it costs less than the cost of one dinner that the management hosts whenever a VIP visits the project. In the absence of a favorable response from the management, the union went on a strike. Questions: a. What are the issues? (03) b. Is the demand of the union justified? (02) c. Evaluate the response of the management. (03) d. Suggest how the problems should be tackled at this stage. (02) (HSS-318) Page 3 of 3

questions.question: Case study 04: One Monday morning Mr. Suhas C.K., a recent from a reputed management institute in Pune walked into the sales office at Chennai as a new sales trainee. Raghavan, the Zonal sales manager for a large computer hardware firm was there to greet him. Raghavan’s job consisted of overseeing the work of sales officer, field executives and trainee salesmen numbering over 50 of three areas namely Chennai, Bangalore, and Trivandrum. The sales growth of companies, parts and other office equipment in his area was highly satisfactory, especially in the recent years-thanks to the developmental initiatives taken by respective State Governments in spreading computer education in offices, schools, and colleges. Raghavan had collected several sales reports, catalogues and pamphlets describing in detail the types of office equipment sold by the company. After a pleasant chat about their backgrounds, Raghavan gave Suhas the collected material and showed him to his assigned desk. Thereafter Raghavan excused himself and didn’t return. Suhas spent the whole day scanning the material and at 5:00pm, he picked up things and went home. a. What do you think about Raghavan’s training programme? (02) b. What type of training programme would you suggest? Justify. (04) c. What method of training would have been best under these (04) circumstances? Would you consider OJT, simulation or experimental methods?

questions.question: Case study 03: Apollo Hospital has been growing in size as it offers quality, prompt-caring services to the patients. Dr. Nitesh Naik, the Administrator is a person with good medical knowledge but lacks the knowledge and skills required in Human Resources Management. The hospital has large quantities of medicine, equipment, spare parts of important machines installed un the hospital. As usual, the hospital has employed a “storekeeper” with no previous experience of Hospital Stores. Mr. Raju, the storekeeper was working earlier in an engineering firm and had sufficient knowledge of such stores. Raju reports to the purchase executive whose job is to order requisite material for requirements of the entire hospital. Dr. Naik has been receiving various complaints from the staff and doctors of non-availability of medicines, drugs, spares of equipment and other consumables required in the hospital having 500 beds. Since, the hospital so far didn’t employ a qualified Personnel Manager, the administrators are not aware of the job analysis procedures , nor they have job description and job specification of any of the jobs being performed. a. Write down the job description, and job specification of a store keeper’s job. (04) b. What are the desirable and essential qualities you think should be mentioned in the job specification? (03) c. Which are the staff members from whom you would collect useful information and requirements for this job? (03) (HSS-318) Page 2 of 3

questions.question: Case study 02: Billy Biscuit company is a medium scale family run company located in Eastern India. It employed 24 workers in the last 2 years. The company had strained industrial relations. When the workers went on strike the company declared a lock out. Four months later the workers union and management resumed dialogue. The union agreed to cooperate with management provided that management lifts the lockout and abolishes the personnel department. The management agreed to both the demands. Question: a. Do you feel that even if the personnel department is abolished, personnel (02) functions should still be carried on? Give reasons. b. What would you have done in order to ensure there was no unionization problem at Billy biscuit company? (02)
